title: Live viewers, and following a match from another device
description: The feed shows how many people are watching, and everybody's screen updates by itself. Nobody has to refresh.
body:
Everybody watching a live match sees the same thing at the same time. Score a goal and it arrives on every screen at once.

Who is watching

  1. Open the match and look at the top of the FEED panel. The green mark counts who has the match open.

  2. Anybody in either squad can open the same match on their own device. The count goes up, with nothing refreshed.

  3. It goes down again when they close it.

Following from another device

Whoever is watching gets the whole match screen, read-only: the score, the clock and the feed. No counters, no card buttons, nothing to press.

When the manager scores, their screen changes on its own.

What you will see

Nobody needs to refresh. Goals, cards, commentary and the clock all arrive by themselves.

Anybody signed in can comment. A follower who cannot change the score can still add a line to the feed. See "The match feed and commentary".

The count is everybody with the match open. Not only your squad, which is why it can be higher than you expect.

The share link needs a Scoryboard account. Sending the match to somebody who is not signed in gets them a sign-in screen, not the match. See "Inviting people, sharing a preview and the matches calendar".

If it does not work

  • The count is not there. Give it a few seconds after the page loads.
  • Somebody says they cannot see the goal. Ask them to check their connection. The match reconnects on its own, so nobody needs to refresh - and refreshing a paused match restarts the clock.
  • They get a sign-in screen instead of the match. They need a Scoryboard account. Invite them to the team.
  • The score on their screen is behind yours. Wait a moment. If it does not catch up, their connection has dropped.
